messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: High queue latency detected for tenant `acme-corp` in Dedicated pool eu-west-1. 95th latency 18s, errors 5% over 5m. Incident severity: P1. @oncall-alice please acknowledge :rotating_light:
oncall-alice: acked. seeing big tail. pulling logs now.
sre-bob: I can join. are they on bespoke batching? last config showed `max_batch_tokens: 4096` and `tenant_queue_weight: 1.0`
eng-runtime-jay: yep, acme requested larger batches for cost. current scheduler knobs: `scheduler.max_batch_tokens=4096`, `scheduler.max_batch_size=64`, `per_tenant_concurrency=8`. queuing depth spiking.
infra-liz: telemetry shows sustained queue depth ~250 for that tenant, fair-share is starving others. overall GPU load at 92%.
customer-support-maya: I just emailed Acme SRE with notice that we're investigating. they report errors in their app (timeouts).
sre-bob: immediate mitigation: reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 for this tenant and lower `tenant_queue_weight` to 0.5 to free up cycles. also set emergency cap `per_tenant_concurrency=4` for acme.
oncall-alice: doing `redwoodctl tenant update acme-corp --set scheduler.max_batch_tokens=1024 scheduler.tenant_queue_weight=0.5 scheduler.per_tenant_concurrency=4` now.
deploy-bot: Started update job 9876 for tenant acme-corp. ETA ~30s.
eng-runtime-jay: while that rolls, enable prefix KV caching bypass for long prefixes? might reduce per-request token work. set `kv_cache.prefer_prefix=false` for tenant.
infra-liz: note: if we lower batch tokens we may increase token-per-request overhead and cost. acceptable for incident.
(25s) deploy-bot: update job 9876 succeeded.
oncall-alice: applied. monitoring...
eng-runtime-jay: immediate improvement on tail latency: 95th down to 6.2s in 1m. errors dropping.
sre-bob: nice. still seeing bursts that queue up — scheduler had backlog of long requests. proposal: add temporary per-tenant FIFO queue with capacity 80 and tune `scheduler.queue_timeout_ms=12000` for acme to expire stuck requests faster.
oncall-alice: can we set `scheduler.max_queue_size=80` for tenant without restart?
eng-runtime-jay: yes via dynamic config API. I'll patch:```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/tenants/acme-corp/config -d '{"scheduler.max_queue_size":80, "scheduler.queue_timeout_ms":12000}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
eng-runtime-jay: patched.
infra-liz: after queue cap set, queue depth dropped to ~40. 95th latency ~4.1s. GPU utilization down to 78%.
customer-support-maya: Acme confirmed app errors cleared. they asked about long-term fix.
se-carlos: long-term: recommend moving Acme to an isolated dedicated pool (reserved) or adjusting batching strategy per workload. For now, record config snapshot and rollback plan.
sre-bob: saving snapshot:```json
{"scheduler.max_batch_tokens":4096, "scheduler.max_queue_size":1000, "per_tenant_concurrency":8, "tenant_queue_weight":1.0}
```
oncall-alice: logged snapshot in incident ticket INC-2026-219. Also attaching perf graphs.
eng-runtime-jay: follow-up actions: 1) run workload replay with smaller max_batch_tokens to measure cost delta; 2) propose a per-tenant adaptive batch knob that reduces `max_batch_tokens` when queue depth > 100; 3) customer offering: upgrade to reserved pool with SLAs.
sre-bob: I'm handing off to dayshift @infra-liz for post-incident cleanup and runbook updates. oncall-alice signing off for sleep.
infra-liz: ack. will run cleanup: increase queue timeout back to default after 2h if stable, schedule meeting with Acme next week, and add a dashboard alert for `per-tenant queue depth > 150`.
customer-support-maya: I'll coordinate customer follow-up and offer interim credits.
oncall-alice: thanks team. :white_check_mark: closing pager, monitoring for 30m then resolve if stable.
(2h later) infra-liz: post-check at +2h: metrics stable, no regressions. reverting `scheduler.queue_timeout_ms` to default and documenting changes in runbook.
(3h) inc-bot: Incident INC-2026-219 auto-closed by infra-liz after verification.
